mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1): "Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidizing agent with bactericidal and keratolytic effects, but the precise mechanism of action is unknown. Tretinoin ... activates three members of the retinoic acid (RAR) nuclear receptors (RARalpha, RARbeta, RARgamma) which act to modify gene expression ... It has not been established whether the clinical effects of tretinoin are mediated through activation of retinoic acid receptors, and/or other mechanisms." A fixed-dose 2-ingredient combination; tretinoin's receptor mechanism is established, benzoyl peroxide's is not.

orange_book.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/orangebook.json, 1 product row matched on products.application_number='214902'. Orange Book lists the current applicant as MAYNE PHARMA LLC, while the FDA label (and CT.gov trial sponsor) name Sol-Gel Technologies/Galderma -- a real post-approval commercial-rights transfer, not a data inconsistency (Twyneo changed hands from originator Sol-Gel to Galderma to Mayne Pharma).

faers_summary.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/event.json aggregate: total_reports=38, serious=2, deaths=0. Brand term TWYNEO has Acne as its clear top real indication (6/38, tied with Product used for unknown indication) -- used as the primary search term since the drug is a 2-ingredient fixed combination with no single clean generic term to query.

drug_characterization.source_excerpt: Computed by pulling every individual FAERS report matching TWYNEO and tallying each report's drugcharacterization code (1=suspect, 2=concomitant, 3=interacting) from ONLY the drug-array entries whose medicinalproduct matches TWYNEO (not co-listed drugs in the same report) -- a plain count= aggregate query cannot do this correctly (openFDA's flattened array indexing mixes in co-listed drugs' own characterization values). 38/38 reports matched.
